entities.summary: Jan Romka was a 13th-century Bishop of Wrocław, serving from 1292 until his death on 19 November 1301. As Bishop, he played a crucial role in the governance of the Archdiocese of Breslau, overseeing the administration of the Catholic Church in the region. Romka was also involved in the political landscape of the region, interacting with local nobles and the Polish monarchy. His tenure coincided with the period of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth's expansion, and he may have played a role in shaping the region's political destiny. Despite the scarcity of information on his personal life, Romka's legacy as a bishop and administrator has endured, with his name appearing in historical records as a testament to his importance in the region's ecclesiastical history. The exact circumstances of his birth and death remain unknown, adding to the enigma surrounding this figure from medieval Eastern Europe.
